title: Terminal / Canvas 2D Text Buffer Reconciler
concept: Host Config Mutation & Canvas Grid Painting
problemStatement: Implement `createGridRenderer(width, height)` that mounts instances with `{ x, y, char }` props onto a 2D character buffer and renders the composed screen string via `renderScreen()`.
interviewTrap: Host configs provide commitMount or finalizeInitialChildren to perform post-insertion side-effects like focusing inputs or painting coordinates.

testCases.name: Mounts character at specific x, y coordinate
testCases.input: place '@' at x: 1, y: 1 in 3x3 grid
testCases.testFn: const r = createGridRenderer(3, 3); const node = r.createInstance('char', { x: 1, y: 1, char: '@' }); r.commitMount(node); return r.renderScreen();

testCases.name: Renders composite 2D grid screen string with multiple instances
testCases.testFn: const r = createGridRenderer(3, 1); r.commitMount(r.createInstance('c', { x: 0, y: 0, char: 'X' })); r.commitMount(r.createInstance('c', { x: 2, y: 0, char: 'O' })); return r.renderScreen();

testCases.name: Ignores out-of-bounds coordinates safely without crash
testCases.testFn: const r = createGridRenderer(3, 1); r.commitMount(r.createInstance('c', { x: 99, y: 99, char: 'Z' })); return r.renderScreen();

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React Reconciler is platform-agnostic. By defining a Host Config object with methods like createInstance, createTextInstance, and appendChild, React can render to Canvas, Three.js, PDF, or Terminal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Host Config Mutation & Canvas Grid Painting.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Host Config Mutation & Canvas Grid Painting maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does a Canvas or Terminal Buffer Reconciler handle layout and character cell painting?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: A terminal or 2D canvas reconciler maintains an in-memory 2D character buffer (e.g. `grid[y][x] = { char, style }`). In `commitUpdate` and `appendChild`, it calculates bounding box offsets (x, y) and writes character cells into the 2D grid array. At the end of the commit phase, it flushes the grid to the terminal using ANSI escape codes or paints to the `<canvas>` via 2D context fillText.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests custom host tree mutation and frame rendering.

howToExplain.opening: A custom canvas/terminal reconciler translates React element trees into 2D grid matrix buffers, flushing assembled frames to terminal or canvas targets.
keyPoints: HostConfig methods map element props to grid cell coordinates.
Commit phase flushes updated cells to screen in one unified draw call.
Enables declarative React development in non-browser environments.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Custom reconcilers prove that React's component model scales far beyond the web browser.
analogies: An LED dot matrix display: components specify which coordinate lights up; the reconciler turns on the exact grid pixels at 60fps.

commonMistakes.mistake: Directly writing to stdout or canvas on every appendChild.
commonMistakes.why: Flushing on every child causes severe screen flickering.
commonMistakes.correct: Buffer changes in memory and flush in resetAfterCommit.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is resetAfterCommit in React Reconciler?
followUpDeepDive.answer: HostConfig hook called once at the conclusion of the commit phase after all mutations are done, ideal for repainting canvas frames or writing terminal buffers.
